thread:
ryan: Heads up — lon2 perf smoke showed a p95 token latency bump when we ramped to steady capacity (~40% higher than our last baseline).
sara: Numbers? which test and cluster?
ryan: ran the standard throughput job (20 nodes, 1 gpu each) for 10m. p50 ~ 120ms (ok), p95 jumped from 360ms baseline -> ~520ms. saw more variance after ~3m. kernel: 6.6.x, nvidia driver reported 535.86 on most nodes.
anya: Were those MIG instances or full GPUs? NVLINK config?
ryan: full GPUs, no MIG. NVLINK enabled. batcher config: target_batch=8, max_latency=50ms.
michael: network telemetry shows a rise in retransmits on leaf-to-tor links around the same time. small snippet from netflow: 
```
LOSS  src=10.10.3.0/24 dst=10.10.4.0/24  p95_rtx=2.3% -> 8.1%  time=2026-02-09T14:07Z
```
infra-bot: Alert: driver-version-mismatch detected across lon2 pool: nodes [gpu-03,gpu-07,gpu-12,gpu-19] running 535.80; rest at 535.86. Kernel modules reloaded at different times.
ops-oncall: @ryan can we isolate to the subset with 535.80 and rerun the p95 test? or run with batcher disabled to see if it’s a scheduling artifact.
ryan: good idea — will re-run on mixed set and also a canary with batcher disabled. command I used: `./perf-run --suite=throughput --nodes=20 --duration=600 --target-batch=8`
sara: quick check on one node: `nvidia-smi -q | grep "Driver Version" -A1` -> returned: 
```
Driver Version : 535.86
Attached GPUs  : 1
```
anya: if network is spiking, KV cache misses + tcp retries could amplify stall tails. try running with KV warm and set target_batch=1 to reduce queuing. also check cgroups/irqbalance.
michael: i'll reimage gpu-03 and gpu-12 (those with 535.80) to sync drivers, schedule for 10m drain window. will report back with kernel dmesg extracts if we see GPU reset or PCI errors.
ryan: cost note — if we fallback to smaller batch sizes to hit p95 target we'll likely increase token cost ~15-25%. flagging for product/cost owners.
ops-oncall: recommend this approach: 1) reimage 2 nodes, 2) rerun small canary (4 nodes), 3) if p95 fixed, roll a staggered reimage across pool, 4) update the bring-up runbook with driver pin check and net telemetry steps.
infra-bot: Runbook draft stub created: `docs/runbooks/lon2-perf-regression.md` (internal).
sara: can you paste the canary command when ready? I’ll run it from my laptop to compare.
ryan: canary command: `./perf-run --suite=throughput --nodes=4 --target-batch=1 --warmup-kv --duration=300` — running now on nodes [gpu-03,gpu-07,gpu-12,gpu-19].
michael: reimage complete for gpu-03/gpu-12. drivers now show 535.86.
ryan: preliminary canary results: p95 back to ~370ms on canary set with batch=1 and warm KV. mixed larger batch rerun still shows volatility on old nodes before reimage.
anya: seems like a coupling between driver mismatch and network retransmits. adding a follow-up to infra checklist: verify driver version parity, check tor rx/tx p95, and run `ethtool -S` health sweep during boot.
ops-oncall: leaving this in your queue @ryan, please file the post-check link in the runbook and tag oncall owners for next 48h. :thumbsup:
ryan: will do — I'll update the runbook with the exact checklist, commands, and cost impact note. thanks all. :wave:
